nodes.name: Webhook: /instagram-post
nodes.notes: Must match N8N_INSTAGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL on the AURON side exactly -- default is http://n8n:5678/webhook/instagram-post, so this node's path must be 'instagram-post'. AURON calls this ONLY after a human has explicitly approved the candidate (see instagram_content/service.py publish()) -- nothing upstream of this webhook makes that decision.

nodes.name: Only single_image (for tonight)
nodes.notes: Tonight's first live test deliberately covers single_image only -- the most common, simplest, lowest-risk case to prove the whole chain end to end. carousel and reel need a second container-per-item + parent-container step (carousel) or the resumable upload protocol (reel/video) -- real but separate additions, not yet wired here. A request with any other post_format falls through to 'Unsupported format -> error response' below rather than silently mishandling it.

nodes.name: Google Drive: Make File Viewable by Link
nodes.notes: Instagram's own media-container step cURLs the image itself -- it must be reachable at a public URL at the moment of the request, AURON never uploads bytes directly. Setting 'anyone with the link, reader' is the minimum needed; the file is NOT indexed or discoverable, only fetchable by anyone who has this exact URL, which only this workflow ever sees.

nodes.name: Instagram: Create Media Container
nodes.notes: AURON_IG_USER_ID and AURON_IG_ACCESS_TOKEN are set as ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES on the n8n container itself (n8n Settings -> Variables, or your docker-compose .env) -- NEVER hardcoded here, NEVER committed to this JSON file. The access token is the long-lived Instagram User token from the Business Login for Instagram flow (graph.instagram.com host -- NOT graph.facebook.com, which rejects this token type with 'Invalid OAuth access token').

nodes.name: Wait for Instagram to Process
nodes.notes: A fixed wait is a reasonable v1 for a single image (usually processes in a few seconds) -- the more correct version polls GET /{container-id}?fields=status_code until it reports FINISHED rather than assuming. Worth upgrading before this handles video/reels, where processing can take much longer and a fixed wait would be unreliable.

nodes.name: Respond: media_id
nodes.notes: AURON's publisher.py reads exactly this field -- 'media_id' -- from the response body. Anything else, or a non-2xx status, is treated as a failed publish (item.status becomes post_failed, a notification goes out) rather than silently assumed successful.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "error": "post_format " + $json.body.post_format + " is not yet wired in this n8n workflow -- only single_image is live tonight." } }}

nodes.name: Unsupported format -> error response
nodes.notes: A clear, honest 422 rather than a silent no-op or a misleading success -- AURON's own publisher.py treats any non-2xx as a real failure and notifies Brano, which is exactly the right behavior here rather than a post that looks approved but never actually went out.
